title: SAML assertion -> RBAC v2 mapping playbook + audit hooks for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we roll out RBAC v2 and stricter admin controls, customers report mismatched role bindings and noisy audit trails when using different IdPs. Root causes include: inconsistent attribute naming, multi-valued group assertions, clock skew causing assertion validity failures, and IdP-level transformations (Okta/Google group filters, Azure AD claim mapping, Ping proxy behaviors).

Goal: Produce an engineering playbook and test artifacts that map SAML assertion shapes from Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping to our RBAC v2 model, define audit logging hooks to preserve assertion metadata for incident/debugging, and add admin UI guardrails to prevent privilege escalation via attribute overrides. Deliverables:
- IdP-specific compatibility notes describing assertion formats we accept and recommended IdP config snippets.
- A canonical SAML-to-RBAC mapping spec (attribute names, precedence, group -> role rules, multi-value handling).
- Audit log schema additions and implementation plan to attach SAML assertion fingerprints to auth events.
- Admin console controls and validation rules to disable IDP claim overrides and surface mapping warnings.
- End-to-end test matrix + synthetic SAML assertions for CI.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Documentation page published in internal docs with sample SAML configs for Okta/Azure/Google/Ping.
2) RBAC engine accepts mapped assertions for the test matrix without role misassignments.
3) Audit logs contain assertion_fingerprint, raw_assertion_id, idp_entity_id, and mapping_diff for every auth event.
4) Admin console prevents saved mappings that could escalate to admin-level permissions unless explicitly approved via a security workflow.

Non-goals: rolling out provider SDKs or changing customer-managed IdP settings automatically.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft spec: https://confluence.internal/redwood/sso-rbac-playbook/draft (placeholder)
- Draft PR for audit schema: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5123 (WIP)
- Test corpus repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sso-test-corpus (branch: eng/ENG-20735)

idp_notes: Okta: Common quirks - admin often uses custom attribute "user.groups" vs. "groups". Okta may emit `nameQualifier` changes when customers use SCIM sync; recommend mapping to normalized 'groups' claim and stripping qualifiers. Also note Okta's default SAML template may omit eduPersonPrincipalName; include snippet to add 'groups' as multi-valued attribute.

Azure AD: Azure emits 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/claims/Group' or 'groups' via Graph. For large group counts, Azure may send only a 'hasgroups' boolean and require Graph calls; document fallback (lookup via SCIM/Graph using service principal) and warn about latency and missing group claims.

Google Workspace: Google uses 'Groups' as a list in 'https://purl.imsglobal.org/spec/lti/claim/roles' or in custom SAML attributes. Customers frequently map email aliases; normalize email claim and prefer immutable 'sub' when available. Google may rewrite NameID formats; accept transient and persistent NameID with mapping rules.

Ping: PingFed sometimes proxies assertions and injects additional attributes (like 'targetedID'); document how to detect proxy chains using Audience and InResponseTo fields and how to prefer original issuer in mapping. Ping deployments often require special entityID allowlists.

Common mitigations: enforce strict clock skew (<5m), validate Recipient/AssertionConsumerService URL, canonicalize group names, limit max groups mapped to roles by default (e.g., 250), and log mapping_diff with redaction of email/PII.
implementation_notes: RBAC engine: add a mapping layer that translates claim bundles into role assignments using ordered precedence: explicit_claim_role > group->role mapping > default_role_for_domain.

Audit trail: store assertion_fingerprint (SHA256 of canonicalized assertion) and mapping_diff (list of granted roles vs. roles requested) as part of the auth event. mapping_diff must be small; truncate > 10k characters and store encrypted blob in audit-store if needed.
Admin controls: UI must surface a 'high-risk mapping' banner if mapping grants roles with scope:admin or scope:datastore.write. High-risk mappings require a secondary approver with 'security' role.
CI: sso-test-corpus will feed assertions into a local SAML consumer and assert final RBAC assignments and audit fields. Add nightly gating job.
risks: Privacy: storing raw assertions may expose PII — require KMS encryption and retention policy (90 days default).
Performance: Azure fallback to Graph for group membership increases auth latency; recommend async population with cached membership to avoid blocking requests.
Customer ops: changes to accepted assertion formats may require customer coordination; prepare rollback plan and support playbook.
